findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: _get_event_stats executes against its scoped_dataset argument, but is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects is called with the closure variable dataset. The dashboard-split factory calls _get_event_stats with discover or another split_dataset while dataset may be metrics_performance/metrics_enhanced_performance, so error split queries are incorrectly judged ineligible and never upsampled; conversely a transaction-like scoped query can inherit eligibility from the outer dataset. Pass scoped_dataset to the eligibility check.

findings.title: upsampled_count drops events whose sample_weight is NULL instead of counting them once
findings.body: The aggregate is sum(sample_weight) with no coalesce/ifNull fallback. Allowlisted projects will contain events without client error sampling (historical events, unsampled/default events, events from SDKs that do not set the context), and any row with NULL sample_weight contributes 0 rather than 1, so enabling upsampling can collapse those buckets to undercounted or zero counts. The new tests only store events with client_sample_rate=0.1 and never cover this case. Use a fallback such as sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1)).

findings.title: Error-focus detection ignores the actual query being executed
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query re-reads request.GET['query'] and only matches the exact substring 'event.type:error'. _get_event_stats receives an explicit query argument that callers modify, e.g. the dashboard-split path builds '({query}) AND !event.type:transaction' and other derived queries, but the helper cannot see those strings, so eligibility is decided from a different query than the one sent to Snuba. It also misses equivalent formatting/casing variations of the executed query. Thread the query argument through is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects/_should_apply_sample_weight_transform instead of reading the request.

findings.title: Internal upsampled_count function is exposed for direct user queries
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction 'upsampled_count' does not set private=True, unlike internal-only functions around it. Because the function converter also resolves user-supplied yAxis values, any caller can request yAxis=upsampled_count() directly for any project or event type, bypassing the allowlist and error-only gating in error_upsampling.py and obtaining weighted counts (or meaningless zeroes where sample_weight is absent). Mark it private so only the server-side column transformation can introduce it.

findings.title: Accidental nested-repository gitlink added to the repository root
findings.body: This adds 'sentry-repo' as a subproject/gitlink pointing at the base commit, with no .gitmodules entry or purpose described in the PR. It is unrelated to upsampling and will pollute the tree, confuse submodule/checkout tooling, and should be removed before merge.

findings.title: Cache invalidation helper is dead code, so allowlist changes have no invalidation path
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is introduced with a docstring saying it should be called when the allowlist configuration changes, but nothing in the PR (or the option-setting machinery) calls it. Eligibility is cached for 60 seconds under a key derived only from organization and project ids, so removing a project from the allowlist keeps returning upsampled counts, and adding one keeps returning raw counts, until TTL expiry, with no way to force consistency. Either wire invalidation into the allowlist change path or remove the helper and document that TTL expiry is the only mechanism.

findings.title: Integration tests miss the errors dataset, topEvents, and unsampled-event cases
findings.body: The new Snuba tests only exercise the default/discover timeseries path with fully sampled events. They do not cover dataset=errors (a branch _should_apply_sample_weight_transform explicitly enables), the separate topEvents transformation branch in _get_event_stats, or an allowlisted project containing events without error_sampling context. Those are exactly the paths where an unregistered function, a missed column transformation, or NULL sample_weight handling would silently fail or return wrong counts, so add cases for them.
